Please capture a terminal recording, so that I can capture exactly what is being output to your terminal.

* Launch wezterm.  If possible, please use the default terminal size of 80x24 cells as it helps to keep things smaller and easier to manage.
* Inside that terminal run `wezterm record` to start a recording session.
* Run through your reproduction steps
* Then type `exit`
* You should see a message like:

```
*** Finished recording to /var/tmp/wezterm-recording-sF6B3u.cast.txt
```

* Attach the file that it produced to this issue.

The file is an asciicast (compatible with https://asciinema.org/) and can also be replayed using `wezterm replay`.

The terminal recording allows me to replicate what is being sent to the terminal without requiring me to install the same applications as you and replicate your configuration for everything.

comments.body: It's telling you that you don't have a font with that glyph. You can follow the instructions in the message to resolve it; either find and install a font that has it, or disable that warning.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
I realized that that is the same codepoint that we were seeing earlier, so I looked into this a bit more.
It seems as though macOS won't tell us which fonts contains U+1f152 when asked about it.
Digging into things a bit more, https://github.com/participant1/wezterm/issues/3546 is a similar issue on Windows.
In there it was discovered that the PingFang font has that codepoint, and that happens to be the same font that macOS will tell wezterm to use when rendering the Chinese characters from your example.

I don't know how to get macOS to return the same result for this particular codepoint, but what you can do to workaround that is to add PingFang to your `font_with_fallback` list explicitly.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: OK, I went back to look at some older logic that we used prior to fixing https://github.com/participant1/wezterm/issues/4099 and found that it could produce a matching font for this codepoint, so I've added that fallback logic as a fallback for this fallback logic(!) and it seems to do the job for your scenario.
